//overrides.why: Security overrides, scoped to the parent that motivates each one. Every entry forces a transitive dependency past a version carrying a high or critical advisory. Verified: 0 high and 0 critical at both full and --omit=dev scope.
//overrides.scoping: These were global and are now parent-scoped, on a reviewer recommendation. The resolved tree is byte-for-byte IDENTICAL either way -- verified by comparing every lockfile node -- so this is a precision change, not a resolution change. The benefit is that each entry now names the parent that justifies it, and a package pulled in later by some other dependency is no longer silently forced.
//overrides.dropped-as-redundant: engine.io (socket.io@4.8.3 already requires ~6.6.0) and brace-expansion (minimatch@10.2.6 already requires ^5.0.8). Both were verified redundant before removal.
//overrides.DANGER: Do NOT remove the minimatch entries while relying on brace-expansion alone. npm audit calls that combination security-equivalent because audit does not execute code -- but minimatch@3.1.5 does `expand = require('brace-expansion')` then `expand(pattern)`, and brace-expansion@5 exports an OBJECT, not a function. It throws `TypeError: expand is not a function` on the first braced pattern ESLint evaluates. An independent review recommended exactly this; architecture review disproved it with a negative control.
//overrides.minimatch-call-convention: minimatch@10's CJS export is a namespace, not callable. ESLint core uses the named .Minimatch export and is safe. Plugin rules calling the default export (react/forbid-component-props, jsx-a11y helpers, several import rules) would throw -- none is currently enabled, so a clean lint run does NOT cover that class.
//overrides.sharp: Runtime, not build-time: Next's image optimizer, invoked under next start. next@16.2.11 declares ^0.34.5 and this EXCEEDS that range on a native module. Unexercised today because the app uses no next/image. Adding next/image makes it load-bearing at request time and requires a smoke test on the deployment Node/OS matrix.
//overrides.postcss: Overrides next's EXACT pin 8.4.31. `npm run build` is this entry's only proof and must stay in the required check set.
//overrides.tar: Scoped to trigger.dev > giget, which declares ^6.2.1 -- this lifts it across the tar 6->7 major. trigger.dev itself already satisfies ^7.5.13 unaided. giget is not referenced anywhere in trigger.dev/dist, so this entry is unexercised.
//overrides.ws: Scoped to engine.io-client, which declares ~8.17.1. This is the live path the Trigger.dev SDK actually uses; the socket.io and engine.io SERVER packages are never imported by this application. Realtime compatibility across this bump is argued, not proven -- see OBL-20.
//overrides.removal-rule: Remove an entry only when its parent's declared range has moved past the advisory, then re-run npm audit at BOTH scopes and npm run lint. Renovate raises these floors automatically but never proposes removal, so nothing but this rule prevents them accumulating.
